title: Odd Even Linked List
statement:
`head` is the first node of a singly linked list. Number the nodes by position starting from 1, so the head sits at position 1 (odd), its successor at position 2 (even), and so on. The parity is about positions, not about the values stored in the nodes.

Relink the list so that every node at an odd position comes before every node at an even position. Within the odd group, and within the even group, nodes keep the order they had originally. Return the head of the relinked list (an empty list stays empty).

Your solution should take O(n) time and use only O(1) extra space.
notes:
## Intuition

The easy way out copies the values into an array, reorders them, and builds a new list, but that costs O(n) extra space. Instead, think of the list as two interleaved chains: odd positions 1, 3, 5, ... and even positions 2, 4, 6, .... Each odd node's new successor is the node two steps ahead, which is exactly the current even node's `next`, and the same holds the other way round. Weaving the two chains apart with two pointers and then attaching the even chain after the odd chain needs only a few variables.

## Approach

1. An empty list is returned as is.
2. Set `odd` to `head`, `even` to `head.next`, and remember the start of the even chain in `evenHead`.
3. While `even` and `even.next` both exist: link `odd.next` to `even.next` and move `odd` there; then link `even.next` to the new `odd.next` and move `even` there.
4. `odd` now ends the odd chain; point it at `evenHead`.
5. Return `head`, which is still the first odd node.

## Example 1, step by step

List `1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5`: `odd = 1`, `even = 2`, `evenHead = 2`.

- Round 1: `1.next = 3`, `odd = 3`; `2.next = 4`, `even = 4`.
- Round 2: `3.next = 5`, `odd = 5`; `4.next = null` (5 has no successor), `even = null`.
- The loop stops. `5.next = evenHead` joins the chains: `1 → 3 → 5 → 2 → 4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each node is relinked once.
- Space: O(1): only four pointers, no matter how long the list is.

## Pitfalls

- Save `evenHead` before the loop; once `head.next` is rewritten, the start of the even chain is lost.
- The loop must test `even.next` too, or `odd` steps onto `null` when the list has an even length and the final link fails.
- Group by position, not by whether `val` is odd or even; example 2 shows the difference.
- Return `head`, not `odd`, which now points at the last odd node.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `odd` | last node of the odd-position chain built so far |
| `even` | last node of the even-position chain built so far |
| `evenHead` | first even node, attached after the odd chain at the end |

narration.2: An empty list has nothing to reorder.
narration.5: The odd chain starts at the head, position 1.
narration.6: The even chain starts at position 2.
narration.7: Remember where the even chain begins; it is attached at the very end.
narration.9: Continue while there is a node after the current even node to hand to the odd chain.
narration.10: The odd node skips over its even neighbour to the next odd position.
narration.12: The even node skips over the new odd node to the next even position.
narration.13: Advance even to that node (possibly null).
narration.15: Join the end of the odd chain to the start of the even chain.
narration.16: The head is still the first odd node, so it heads the reordered list.
